title: Chevron Begins Drilling New Well at Egypt's Narges Gas Field - The Globe and Mail
content: Chevron CorporationCVX has launched a new drilling operation in Egypt’s Mediterranean-based Narges natural gas field, marking a significant milestone in its long-term expansion strategy across the Eastern Mediterranean energy sector. The drilling campaign highlights the growing importance of Egypt as a regional natural gas powerhouse while reinforcing Chevron’s ambition to substantially increase production capacity in one of the world’s most strategically valuable energy regions. The drilling operation commenced aboard the advanced drillship “Stena Forth,” which recently arrived in Egyptian waters to begin exploration and development work at the offshore concession. The Narges field is operated by CVX in partnership with Italy’s Eni S.p.A.E, the UAE’s Mubadala Energy and Egypt’s Tharwa Petroleum Company. The collaboration demonstrates the increasing confidence international energy giants have in Egypt’s offshore natural gas reserves and the country’s expanding role within global energy markets. Egyptian minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi personally inspected the launch of operations, emphasizing the government’s commitment to accelerating production from undeveloped offshore gas discoveries. The Egyptian government considers projects such as Narges essential for increasing domestic energy security, reducing reliance on imports and strengthening the country’s broader economic position amid rising energy demand. Egypt has intensified efforts to maximize domestic natural gas production as part of a broader national strategy designed to stabilize local energy supplies and minimize the financial burden associated with importing fuel. The development of the Narges field represents a major component of this strategy, particularly as Egypt seeks to balance growing domestic consumption with its ambitions to remain a leading regional energy exporter. Badawi praised CVX and its partners for maintaining close coordination with the Egyptian petroleum sector and the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company to overcome operational challenges and accelerate offshore drilling plans. Egyptian authorities are increasingly focused on bringing undeveloped discoveries into production as quickly as possible, particularly in the Mediterranean basin, where several promising gas reserves have been identified in recent years. The Narges field is viewed as a strategically important asset capable of enhancing Egypt’s natural gas supply network while supporting industrial growth, electricity generation and long-term energy stability. Expanding local production remains a top priority for the Egyptian government as it seeks to reduce exposure to global energy market volatility and rising import costs. The launch of drilling activities at the Narges field further elevates the importance of the Eastern Mediterranean as one of the world’s fastest-growing natural gas exploration regions. Over the past decade, massive offshore discoveries across the Mediterranean have transformed the regional energy landscape and attracted substantial investments from international oil and gas companies. Egypt has emerged as a dominant player within this evolving energy corridor due to its extensive infrastructure, strategic geographic position and supportive investment environment. The country’s existing LNG export terminals provide a significant advantage by enabling the rapid commercialization of offshore discoveries and facilitating exports to European and global markets. The Narges project also reinforces Egypt’s position as a critical energy bridge connecting Africa, the Middle East and Europe. As European nations continue seeking diversified natural gas suppliers amid geopolitical uncertainty and supply disruptions, Eastern Mediterranean gas projects have gained increasing international relevance. Chevron’s investment in the Narges field reflects broader industry confidence in the commercial viability of Mediterranean offshore exploration. The company views Egypt and the wider Eastern Mediterranean region as essential pillars within its future operational roadmap. Chevron’s drilling operations at Narges align closely with its broader strategic objective of significantly increasing production capacity throughout the Eastern Mediterranean over the next five years. During the Egypt Energy Show, Clay Neff, president of Exploration Operations at Chevron, confirmed plans to deepen its regional presence through additional offshore drilling campaigns and expanded exploration activities. According to Neff, Chevron intends to increase operational output in the region by as much as 50%, with Egypt playing a central role in achieving that target. In addition to the Narges field, CVX is also pursuing further exploration projects in the Western Mediterranean in partnership with Shell plcSHEL, highlighting its aggressive expansion strategy in offshore gas development. The decision to scale up operations reflects growing global demand for natural gas as countries transition toward cleaner-burning energy alternatives. Natural gas continues to play a critical role in international energy systems, particularly as governments seek to balance economic growth, energy security and emissions reduction goals. Chevron’s expansion strategy also underscores its confidence in Egypt’s long-term investment climate. Stable regulatory frameworks, established infrastructure and strong cooperation between international operators and Egyptian authorities have created favorable conditions for sustained offshore development. Egypt’s offshore energy sector is attracting increasing global attention as international energy companies race to secure opportunities in the Eastern Mediterranean. The successful development of large-scale projects such as Zohr previously demonstrated the immense geological potential of the region, encouraging additional exploration and investment activity. The Narges field may become another transformative asset capable of strengthening Egypt’s role as both a major producer and exporter of natural gas. Industry analysts believe continued exploration success across the Mediterranean basin could significantly enhance Egypt’s influence within international energy markets over the coming decade. The country’s advanced LNG export infrastructure remains one of its strongest competitive advantages. Unlike many emerging gas-producing nations, Egypt already possesses operational export facilities capable of connecting offshore production directly to international buyers. This infrastructure allows newly discovered reserves to move toward commercialization more rapidly than in less developed regions. At the same time, Egypt’s strategic location offers direct access to European energy markets, which remain highly focused on securing diversified and reliable gas supplies. As global competition for energy resources intensifies, Egypt’s offshore sector is becoming increasingly valuable from both economic and geopolitical perspectives. The continued development of the Narges field is expected to generate substantial economic benefits for Egypt while supporting long-term growth across the domestic energy industry. Increased offshore production can help reduce the country’s dependence on imported fuel while improving overall energy reliability for industrial and residential consumers. The project is also expected to contribute to higher government revenues through taxes, royalties and export earnings. Expanding offshore activity supports employment opportunities across multiple sectors, including engineering, logistics, maritime services, transportation and energy infrastructure development. For Chevron and its partners, the Narges field represents an opportunity to capitalize on rising international demand for natural gas while strengthening their positions within one of the world’s most promising offshore exploration regions. Continued success in Egypt’s Mediterranean waters could encourage further investment and unlock additional discoveries capable of reshaping the region’s energy future. Chevron’s latest drilling campaign at the Narges field signals a major step forward for Egypt’s offshore natural gas ambitions. With strong international partnerships, advanced export infrastructure and increasing government support for exploration activities, Egypt is positioning itself as a dominant force within the Eastern Mediterranean energy landscape. As drilling operations progress and production development accelerates, the Narges field could become a key contributor to Egypt’s domestic energy strategy and export capabilities. Chevron’s long-term commitment to expanding regional production further confirms the strategic significance of Egypt within the evolving global natural gas market. The coming years are expected to bring intensified exploration activity, additional foreign investment and expanded offshore development projects throughout the Mediterranean basin. Egypt’s ability to rapidly advance discoveries such as Narges into production may ultimately define its future role as one of the world’s most influential emerging energy hubs. title: Brent Crude Is Up 85% Since January. OXY, XOM, and CVX Are Playing It Very Differently. - AOL.com
content: Oil prices have risen dramatically in 2026, driven higher by the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East. Some of the most important oil companies didn't benefit as much as you would expect because of regional exposure, timing, and hedging activity. 10 stocks we like better than Occidental Petroleum › Occidental Petroleum (NYSE: OXY) beat Wall Street estimates by a wide margin when it reported first-quarter 2026 earnings. Analysts were expecting earnings of $0.59 per share, but the company reported $1.06 per share. That's an impressive beat, but management admits that it could have done better. What's going on with the company and with peers like Chevron (NYSE: CVX) and ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM)? One of the first big problems in the quarter for oil companies was the timing of the oil price spike. Most of the advance occurred after the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East began, so the spike that has pushed oil prices up 85% in 2026 as of this writing didn't really get underway until March. So, energy companies only benefited from higher oil prices for a short period. Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? For example, Wall Street is projecting Oxy to earn $1.58 per share in the second quarter. But another issue hampered Oxy's performance in the first quarter: hedging. Oil companies routinely hedge their production to protect against price movements in energy markets. In this case, that hedging turned into a headwind. Oxy, which is much less exposed to the Middle East than Exxon or Chevron, was a relative standout. At the other extreme was Exxon, which has more exposure to the region and saw its production impacted. That said, its $1.16 per share in earnings beat the analyst call of $1.01. But hedging led to a $700 million earnings hit. That should be reversed in the second quarter as shipments hedged are delivered. Still, the short-term impact is worth noting as you examine the business. Chevron, meanwhile, fell between Exxon and Oxy, with its $1.41 per share earnings beating Wall Street's $0.97 per share call. But once again, the company's hedging activity was a headwind, as management took a $2.9 billion charge related to it. Hedging is company-specific, with each company adopting a different approach. And because hedging is a proprietary activity, investors won't know about the impact, good or bad, until the company releases quarterly results. That said, the refining operations of Exxon and Chevron performed weakly, with timing and hedging both playing a role. Oxy recently sold its downstream business at the start of 2026, so this business wasn't a meaningful issue for the company in the quarter. Simply put, there are a lot of moving parts to consider when you look at individual energy companies. In the end, Oxy, Exxon, and Chevron are all benefiting from rising energy prices, but the way they are playing the rise is slightly different. And that, in turn, is leading to different outcomes. As policy debates on energy security, decarbonization, and geopolitical exposure continue, investors are watching how large oil and gas companies handle country specific scrutiny. title: My 2 Favorite Warren Buffett Stocks for May - The Globe and Mail
content: The Berkshire Hathaway portfolio received a shake-up in Q1 from new CEO Greg Abel. Chevron and Apple remain top-5 holdings in the Berkshire portfolio. Warren Buffett is no longer running day-to-day operations at Berkshire Hathaway, but he remains on as board chairman and built much of the company's existing portfolio of stocks and investments, although his successor, Greg Abel, made some wholesale changes in his first quarter as CEO. The current portfolio is a mix of "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks, banks and financial giants, consumer staples, and energy leaders. But there are two Buffett stocks that stand out right now as terrific buys in the month of May. Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue » Gas prices have been soaring since the war in Iran began and the Strait of Hormuz closed. Without getting into the mechanics, the closure has created a supply deficit, which, in turn, has led to higher oil prices and higher consumer costs. In the first quarter, Chevron(NYSE: CVX) only saw about a 2% increase in revenue and a 37% decline in earnings. But the pedestrian numbers are mostly due to the timing effects related to shipping and accounting. The true telltale sign that Chevron had a great quarter was its production, which increased by some 500,000 barrels per day, including 388,000 barrels per day in the U.S., mostly in the Permian Basin and the Gulf, and 117,000 per day internationally. Overall, it's about a 15% increase year over year. This jump is reflected in its guidance, which calls for 7% to 10% production growth this fiscal year -- and higher production means there is more to sell, and that leads to higher revenue. In addition, Chevron gets more of its oil from the U.S. than from the Middle East, so there is the potential for less disruption while the war in Iran drags on. These factors, along with its strong adjusted free cash flow of $4.1 billion in Q1 2026, has helped spike Chevron's stock price some 28% year to date. And with its robust earnings outlook, the forward price-to-earnings (P/E) is just 14, while the five-year price/earnings-to-growth (PEG) ratio is in value territory at 0.84. Finally, there is the dividend. With an abundance of free cash flow and a robust outlook, Chevron has been adding to its already excellent dividend. It increased its dividend for the 39th straight year in 2026, paying out a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share at a yield of 3.63%. At a time of significant uncertainty over valuations and the economy, Chevron stock, a Buffett favorite, is a good defensive play. Apple(NASDAQ: AAPL) has long been Buffett's largest holding, but he had been consistently shedding shares for the past few years. In Q1, Abel did not sell any more Apple stock, keeping its roughly 228 million shares intact. Apple remains the largest position in Berkshire's portfolio, accounting for about 22% of the $263 billion portfolio. That could certainly be viewed as a vote of confidence for Apple stock, which is up about 10% year to date and 42% over the past 12 months (at the time of this writing). Apple is coming off a great quarter where it delivered record fiscal Q2 revenue fueled by demand for the iPhone 17. Revenue increased 17%, while earnings spiked 22%. And for the June quarter, Apple's fiscal Q3, Apple anticipates revenue rising 14% to 17%, which is better than analysts' expectations. May is a particularly good time to buy Apple shares because these are the weeks leading up to its annual Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) on June 8. Apple stock typically gets a boost leading up to the WWDC, its biggest event of the year where it often rolls out new products and services. This year, it is introducing several new AI-related features for the iPhone and other products to improve accessibility. These features include voiceover, magnifier, voice control, reading summaries, video captions, and the ability for users to control wheelchairs with their eyes, among other features. Also, Bloomberg reported that Apple is reorganizing its hardware development business to accelerate the launch of new products. While Apple typically gets a buy-the-rumor boost leading up to WWDC, there is sometimes the knee-jerk sell-the-news reaction. But with its reasonable valuation, sales increases, and the transition to new CEO John Ternus in September, who comes from the hardware engineering department and should signal a shift toward product development, there is a lot of positive momentum at Apple.
